evidence: The survivor uses "order vertices by decreasing degree" followed by recursive "dfs(pos)", with no memoization, component decomposition, or strong pruning.
affordance_in_statement: Every interference pair must be assigned "strictly different frequency bands," while the statement provides no structural restriction on the interference graph; thus the task is unrestricted 3-colorability.
removal_suggestion: The unrestricted 3-colorability core cannot be removed without changing the task. Re-present the scenario explicitly as an adversarial interference log capable of encoding arbitrary hard 3-colorability instances, rather than suggesting ordinary engineering data.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses degree-ordered recursive backtracking as a general-purpose 3-coloring solver.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Every interfering pair must use different values from the three bands, with no promise of an easy graph structure.

common_affordance: The input is unrestricted 3-colorability, so a generic degree-ordered DFS/backtracking solver can be attempted.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its recursive backtracking coloring search has exponential worst-case behavior and times out on adversarial 40-vertex graphs.
It likewise relies on unoptimized recursive 3-coloring backtracking, causing exponential search and TLE on hard instances.

recommended_edit: Add to the scenario that the resonance log is adversarial and may encode arbitrary deliberately hard 3-colorability instances, including worst-case yes and no cases, so naive exhaustive coloring is not viable.
